newsitem.title: USA: Judge upholds Marvel bondholders control.
newsitem.headline: Judge upholds Marvel bondholders control.

text.p: A judge has upheld a lower court ruling giving bondholders of Marvel Holdings Inc control of the company so that they can vote the shares of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc, which secures the $894 million face value of their bonds.

At a hearing Thursday before Judge Roderick McKelvie of the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Marvel and its banks, led by Chase Manhattan Corp, sought to have reversed the bankruptcy court's February 26 ruling allowing bondholders, led by Carl Ichan, to foreclose on and vote the pledged shares.

Marvel has until 5 p.m. tomorrow to prove to U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick that without an order blocking the bondholders from taking control, the estate and therefore the creditors of the company will suffer irreparable harm.
During the hearing, Marvel attorney Harvey Miller told Judge McKelvie that a possible merger with Toy Biz Inc was in the works.
"There has been extensive negotiations...I am told the banks (Chase) and Toy Biz are very close to an agreement," Miller said.
Toy Biz attorney Robert Mittman told Reuters, "I cannot confirm one way or the other" Miller's comments about the merger talks.

Marvel spokesman Michael Freitag said after the hearing: "Naturally we're disappointed by the judge's ruling, but we respect it. We will now explore what options remain to ensure that the current Marvel Entertainment board will have the opportunity to resolve this chapter 11 case in a manner that serves the best interests of all the parties."
At present there are two competing reorganization plans for allowing Marvel Entertainment to emerge from chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
Ichan's bondholder plan calls for an infusion of $365 million to be used for ongoing operations, or for satisfying claims.
Under a plan proposed by Marvel and its banks, which are the senior secured lenders of Marvel Entertainment, Marvel Entertainment and its affiliates would be auctioned off.

Until such time that the bondholders actually take control of the 80 percent of Marvel Entertainment shares securing their claim, those shares remain in the control of Ronald Perelman who is on the board of Marvel Entertainment.
There will be a hearing on July 17 in the bankruptcy court to determine the adequacy of the disclosure statements for both plans.
The disclosure statement provides financial information that an investor can use to make an informed decision about whether to accept a reorganization plan.
McKelvie declined Miller's request that the court order the bondholders and the banks to submit to mediation, saying the court has no authority to do so.
